claim: T-V4-63 (V04 l. 3156), rewritten this round by R6-02's (V4-8) with VV34-r5-02, adds two clauses that leave an arch vault `collapsed` under a fallen span: 'the circuit's case run again with that `vault` span breached with its chamber first (`ruined`, its arch vault `collapsed`) … (§2.7's crossing table, W1·C6)', and the frame growth's 'each new span taking that end span's `state` … a vault laid in a `ruined` or `cleared` one `collapsed` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2))'. Its bar, kept from round 4, still reads 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a standing span of use `vault`'. In the set a standing span is one whose `state` is absent (V06 §3.19.1 (3) 'every span standing or ruined'; V06 §3.19.2 (3) 'each standing span … → breach'; V06 §3.2 l. 1038 'a chamber for each standing `vault` span …, a collapse under a `ruined` or `cleared` span'). V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2)–(3) keep a collapsed vault in a ruined or cleared span; only a span gone, set `open` or under a wall removes it. So after the breach commit and after the frame growth's commit the test's own fixtures hold a collapsed vault keyed to a `ruined` span, and the bar fails on a correct build. One builder keeps the bar and suppresses those vaults, against (d) (1)–(2) and the clause's own words; another reads 'standing' as 'existing'. Two builds.
required_change: T-V4-63's bar 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a standing span of use `vault`' → 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a span of the way whose `use` is `vault` and over which no wall stands — standing, or `ruined` or `cleared` with that vault `collapsed` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2))'.

claim: The round's sweep put "no wall stands over" (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1)) on every restatement of the lay rule except two clauses of T-V4-63's own bar (l. 3156). The sweep covered §1b.3, §4.1, §4.2, §4.6, T-V4-62, and T-V4-63's "a user-added raised way's `vault` spans" and "each new `vault` span". The first missed clause is "a span's `use` edit lays or removes exactly that vault and survives a regeneration": on a span under a wall a `use` set to `vault` lays nothing (§1b.3 l. 370, §4.2 l. 2557: "none in a span a wall stands over"). The second is the frame growth's "with the same id and footprint, the arch vault of every old `vault` span between two of them". The span rule never reads a wall (base l. 2733–2736), so a span between two old stations under a ring the old deck crosses can be `vault` in its record yet holds no vault (base l. 2746). Read literally, both clauses expect a vault that a correct build never lays, and the same bar's next clause ("no chamber stands … in a `vault` span a wall stands over") contradicts them. The mechanism is (d) (1)'s, so nothing built changes.
required_change: T-V4-63: "a span's `use` edit lays or removes exactly that vault and survives a regeneration" → "a span's `use` edit lays or removes exactly that vault (none in a span a wall stands over, V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1)) and survives a regeneration"; and "the arch vault of every old `vault` span between two of them (§2.7's support step (7))" → "the arch vault of every old `vault` span between two of them that no wall stands over (§2.7's support step (7); V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1))".

claim: R6-07 puts "and under no disaster look" on every "never decayed ⇒ unchanged" statement (item 122 (d)). The round wrote the condition on the building subject of UE33's E1 (l. 2435) and on T-V4-82 (g)'s never-decayed control (l. 3175). It did not write it on their second subject: E1's "an underground none of whose buildings has decayed" and (g)'s "every band of an underground with no decayed building", each said to draw (and export) byte-identically. Under a look, a storey below 0 reads its building's drawn level, the higher of its own and the look's (J-V4.130; V04 §5.6 (6): "the look over a storey below 0 with V03 §5.6 (4)'s"). T-V4-82 (i) draws a never-decayed church's crypt at the look's level. So such an underground is not byte-identical while a look stands over it. T-V4-82 (i) runs the look, and (g)'s fixture holds none, so nothing built or tested changes.
required_change: UE33's E1: "and an underground none of whose buildings has decayed, draw byte-identically" → "and an underground none of whose buildings has decayed or stands under a disaster look, draw byte-identically". T-V4-82 (g): "and every band of an underground with no decayed building draw and export byte-identically" → "and every band of an underground with no decayed building and none under a disaster look draw and export byte-identically".

claim: One fix with VV56-r6-02 (major, model), at a V04 site its END list does not name (that END names only §3.10's bullet, l. 2285–2294). V04 §1b.2's `ArchVaults.reconcile` trigger list (l. 328) is the list §2.6's arch-vault row cites as the commits that remove or lay a vault under a wall. It names "an absorbed record dropped". No op drops a cleared enceinte record: `absorbWall` takes it to existence `cleared` and keeps it (V06 l. 717; V06 §3.7.2 (3), l. 1488–1499: "the fortification phase keeps the cleared record in its loop … until every run is `dismantled`", then the `enceinte` provider reads it). The same cell's general words ("the commit of every enceinte band or wall strip laid, moved or removed over a `vault` span's under-deck strip") make `absorbWall`'s own commit the trigger, since its strips re-join the blocks (V06 §2.8's op comment). A hand `convert` `absorbWall` (T3 `wall`'s convert kinds, base l. 10588; the crossing table's W8·C9) runs no `EpochScope.raised`, so l. 328 alone decides it. One builder re-lays the vault in the absorb's commit; another waits for an event no op makes.
required_change: V04 §1b.2's trigger cell (l. 328): "`wallToWay`, an absorbed record dropped;" → "`wallToWay`, `absorbWall` (in its commit, its strips merged into the blocks);", written with VV56-r6-02's ruling of the crossing table's W8·C2. If that ruling names another event, l. 328 names the same one in W8's words.

claim: T-V4-63 (l. 3156) has clauses that run on V06's epoch ops: "an epoch that founds a raised way (V06's `under.extend`) lays its vaults in the epoch's commit"; "passed beneath by an epoch circuit" (V06 §3.7; the crossing table's W1: "an epoch's circuit … (V06 §3.7)"); and, new this round, "the circuit's case run again with that `vault` span breached with its chamber first" (a `DeclineOp` breach, which E3 builds, as R6-09 schedules T110-2's lapse). V04 §8's U5 cell (l. 3210) runs T-V4-63 whole at U5, where V04 runs the epoch reconcile "by hand and on M4's grow path". V06's `under.*` adapters, which run the arch-vault reconcile over `EpochScope.raised`, land at V06's E8 (V06 §8's E8 row), and INDEX §4 puts E8 after V04's U5. So these clauses are scheduled before their provider: R6-09's class (INDEX §5 risk 2; R5-05 (c)), the mirror of VAT6-r6-03's V06 clauses. Nothing built changes.
required_change: V04 §8's U5 tests cell: "T-V4-63, T-V4-70" → "T-V4-63 (its clauses on V06's epoch ops — the founding, the epoch circuit and its run with the span breached first — at V06's E8, which builds `under.extend`'s reconcile over `EpochScope.raised`), T-V4-70".
